newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Jan export prices up 1.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Jan export prices up 1.0 pct.

text.p: Australia's export prices rose 1.0 percent in January from the previous month, and were 6.0 percent lower than a year before, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Tuesday.
"Prices for aluminium and aluminium goods increased during the month, reflecting increases in the world market price of aluminium," the bureau said in a statement.
"A decrease in the value of the Australian dollar against the U.S. dollar led to increases in the prices of coal and iron ore."
These increases were partially offset by price decreases for gold and refined petroleum, the bureau said.
The biggest monthly rise was in base metals and articles of base metals, which rose 5.3 percent, for an annual fall of 11 percent.
The biggest fall was in gold, diamonds and coin, which fell 2.9 percent, for an annual fall of 15.5 percent.
It was the first monthly rise since August last year. Prices fell every month last year except in August and January.
